o: Table Days holds one date per row and each must be re-emitted as "Tuesday, April 12, 2022" style text: full weekday name, full month name, a day number WITHOUT a leading zero, and the exact comma-and-space punctuation shown in the example. The sample rows map to "Monday, August 9, 2021" for 2021-08-09 (note the bare 9) and "Friday, June 26, 2020" for 2020-06-26. MySQL does all of the work inside DATE_FORMAT with the pattern "%W, %M %e, %Y"; the subtle part is choosing %e instead of %d, which would render "09". A dialect-portable alternative concatenates the components manually, translating numeric weekday and month values through ELT lookup lists.
k: %W / %M / %e / %Y cover weekday name, month name, zero-free day number, and year in a single DATE_FORMAT call.
%d pads the day to two digits ("09") while %e does not — exact-match output demands %e.
Keep the expression aliased AS day so the result schema still has the expected column name.

a.i: One formatting call maps each stored date to the required display string; MySQL resolves names and casing internally. This is the idiomatic solution to give first.
s: Alias the expression AS day so the output column keeps its original name.

a.n: Approach 2: Manual CONCAT with ELT Lookups
a.i: Compute every component numerically and translate it explicitly: WEEKDAY(day) + 1 indexes the Monday-first list of weekday names, MONTH(day) indexes the twelve months, and DAYOFMONTH/YEAR are already plain numbers. This spells out the logic and ports easily to engines without DATE_FORMAT-style pattern codes.
s: Alias the whole CONCAT expression AS day.

c.python:
-- Database problem — the accepted submission is a single MySQL query:
SELECT CONCAT(
         ELT(WEEKDAY(day) + 1,
             'Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'),
         ', ',
         ELT(MONTH(day), 'January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June',
             'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December'),
         ' ',
         DAYOFMONTH(day),
         ', ',
         YEAR(day)
       ) AS day
FROM Days;

w: Lead with DATE_FORMAT; bring up CONCAT/ELT only if the interviewer probes portability across dialects. Classic traps: using %d instead of %e (the leading zero fails exact-match graders), confusing WEEKDAY() (Monday = 0) with DAYOFWEEK() (Sunday = 1) when indexing the ELT lists, and dropping the alias so the column is no longer named day. Follow-ups: express the same format in PostgreSQL (TO_CHAR) or SQL Server (DATENAME + CONVERT), or add locale-aware month names.
